item.title: Ralliston's Journey through all of the 001 proposals - Part Five - Roget's Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Review: Hmm… I dunno. I'm not the biggest fan of this one. I feel like it depends too much on the crosslinking. And whilst I know that's the whole point of it, an article must stand on its own. I will, however, say that the 'self-containments' table was really nicely and creatively done; I really liked it.

When the 'this is the source of all Keters' part came up, I was really excited to read forward, as I thought the final 'plot twist' is going to be that Keter Duty was created by a previous Foundation / a Foundation from an alternate really or something like that to help secure this one but, unless I'm missing something, that wasn't the case; I will say that I really, really don't understand the message, which might be the source of my confusion. Maybe I will re-visit this one sometime in the future and then I might get something I'm currently missing - for now, however, this lands rather mediocrely.

Edit: Oh. OH. OOOOOOH. Alright, upon reading the declass, it makes so much more sense. This is goddamn phenomenal.

Result: No-vote +1

item.content:encoded:
Nice scip, but I wonder how to reconcile it with the rest of the potential SCPverse. I mean, take 682 for example; how can it be contained in SCP-001 when the SCP-682 article says it's contained at a persumably different site under hydrochloric acid immersion? Or was it moved to SCP-001 after the lengthy history of containment breaches described in the -682 article?

All four SCP-1295 entities are continuously served instances of SCP-871 by a blond human woman in a waitress outfit, who continuously retrieves instances of SCP-871 from a wooden table and brings them to the SCP-1295 entities.

… Who is this "blond human woman in a waitress outfit"? She's not part of either SCP's description, and the description of this entry implies that she's doing this constantly and without rest, which could only be possible if she herself was an anomalous entity as well.

item.content:encoded:
I just realised something, but i'm probably completely wrong.

Despite the proposal containing some of the most popular SCP's on the site, SCP-076 isn't represented anywhere. I was a bit like "Aww, that's a missed opportunity right there". Then I reread 076's file, specifically the Classified Warning:

All information regarding Project Able and Mobile Task Force Omega-7 ("Pandora's Box") are classified Q Clearance by order of the O-5 Council.

And then I reread the addendum at the bottom of Roget's Proposal:

If you see the seventh bride, tell her I'm sorry she had to open the box. Maybe she'll remember it.

The unnamed anomaly that was neutralised by [REDACTED] (The Scarlet King?) is Mobile Task Force Omega-7, code named Pandora's box. Presumably Able and the Scarlet King fought to the death, causing something terrible to happen if Procedure 110-Montauk isn't carried out correctly.

The only problem with this theory is the fact the unnamed entity in the proposal only has two black bars rather than the three needed for "076".

Anyway, this is one of my favourite 001 proposals, and a great read in general, +1!

item.content:encoded:
Most of this I like (love about 3/4 of the cross-testing!), but the realization that cost my upvote (still can't bring myself to downvote) is that all of those Iconic SCPs would be out of circulation. That's not a problem, except by the framework given for the SPC 001 entries. If this was the true SCP 001, then the disappearance of some of the best known and feared SCPs would likely be known in the Foundation, making decoy files pointless. If this were a decoy, it would be obvious for the same reason. These objects have some of the most personnel-intensive containment, making their presence or absence unambiguous.
This might work better if it were a piece of documentation recovered from a strange source that might be a preceding or subsequent iteration of reality. The hope/cautionary tale that this could be done might be enough for the O5s to hide it there, and it would allow for the fun idea of multiple 001s being simultaneously true.
